summary: Aleksandra Turek is an Indologist who earned her M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Warsaw (1996-2009). She became an assistant professor there in 2010.

Aleksei Davydovich Litman worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Moscow State University (~1945-1950). He served as Secretary at the Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan (1951-1956) and as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies from 1957.

Aleksei Dyakov specialized in Indology and history/archaeology, studying at Moscow State University (1913-1914, ~1916-1921) and Tomsk State University (1914-1919). In 1950, he was a professor at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Aleksei Osipovich Ivanovskii specialized in Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1881) under Vasily Vasiliev, Aleksey Pozdneev, and Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, and succeeded Sergey Georgiyevsky in 1894.

Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov studied at Kyiv University (~1910-1914) under Friedrich Knauer, Sergey Oldenburg, and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. An Indologist and linguist, he became professor at Saint Petersburg State University (1929) and director of the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1938-1940, 1946-1952).

Aleksej Stepanovič Barhudarov was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1945-1950). He was a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1953-1971) and joined the Institute of Linguistics in 1971.

Aleksey Sergeevich Sukhochev was an Indologist who studied at Moscow State University (~1952-1957). In 1956, he became a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
Aleksey Shakhmatov studied under Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov and Theodor Korsch between approximately 1879 and 1883.

Indologist Alessandro Giudice studied at the University of Pisa (MA 2020-2022) and University of Cagliari (PhD 2022-2026). His posts include cultore della materia at Pisa (2023) and Cagliari (2025), and Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy (attested 2026).

Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. He has served as a university assistant at the University of Vienna and principal investigator at IKGA (both attested 2022), and as assistant professor at the University of Toronto (attested 2026).
Alessandro Veniero worked in linguistics and Indology. He held a professorship at the University of Catania in 1917 and served as principal at the Liceo di Macerata from 1918 to 1919.

Alex McKay is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London by 1995. His career includes fellowships at University College London, the International Institute for Asian Studies, and SOAS as Millennium Research Fellow.

Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy, having studied at Oxford, SOAS, and under Alexis Sanderson, Harunaga Isaacson, and Ernst Steinkellner. His appointments include Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2006), Harvard University, and Ashoka University (attested 2018-2020).

Alex Wayman was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who earned his PhD at UC Berkeley (~1953-1959) under Ferdinand Lessing. He held faculty posts at UC Berkeley, Wisconsin-Madison, and Columbia University.

Alexander B. Nicholson studied at Princeton Theological Seminary (B.A. 1864). An Indologist and linguist, he served as Cedar Hill School principal (1876) and was Professor of Comparative Philology and Sanskrit at Queen's University of Ireland from 1902.

Alexander Berzin, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned degrees from Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard (~1965-1972) under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He co-founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives translation bureau (~1972-1974) and studied under several Tibetan masters.

Alexander Coburn Soper specialized in Sinology, Japanology, and archaeology, completing his B.A. at Hamilton and M.A. and Ph.D. at Princeton. He held professorships at Bryn Mawr (1946) and NYU (1960), and edited Artibus Asiae (1958-1993).

Alexander Cunningham studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary and under James Prinsep. Working in Indology and archaeology, he founded the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as Archaeological Surveyor (1861-1865) and its first Director-General (1871-1885).
Alexander Duff was an author in religious studies and history who studied at the University of St Andrews (~1821-1829) and the University of Aberdeen, later teaching Krishna Mohan Banerjee.
Alexander Duncan Campbell was an Indologist and linguist active in the Madras Literary Society. In 1816, he served on the Board of Superintendence at the College of Fort St. George.
